why: Figure 1 is one circle and figure 2 shows circles overlapping side by side. Figure 3 is one square, so figure 4 should show squares overlapping side by side. In option 1 the small square overlaps the big square on its side. In options 2 and 4 the squares do not touch, and in option 3 they overlap on top.
trick: Think in pairs: what figure 2 does to figure 1, figure 4 does to figure 3.
